deep.gist: The video reviews a dense week of AI releases, including a camera-path video generator, an Nvidia video upscaler, two very small transcription models, and Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 5.5. It also opens with mentions of Gemini 4 Argon, OpenAI Dev Day, and a new Dots product, then ends while beginning the Dots segment.
key_points: In Spatial World 1.5 takes an image plus a camera path and generates a video walking through the scene along that path.
In Spatial World 1.5 can start from a single image, multiple images, a panorama, or a full video, and can capture motion from the input video.
In Spatial World 1.5 allows frame freezing for bullet time effects and has released code with download and run instructions.
In Spatial World 1.5 is based on a 1.3b model and is under 6 GB in size, so it can run on most consumer GPUs.
Nvidia's Soul Refiner upscales low-resolution video to sharper high-resolution video up to 4K in a single step.
Soul Refiner is model agnostic and can be used with video models such as Miniax H3, Nvidia Cosmos, or Alibaba 1.
Soul Refiner is sharper than the original video but can alter details, making it not fully faithful to the source footage.
Soul Refiner is borrowed from the LTX Refiner and fine-tuned to perform upscaling in one step.
A tiny speech-to-text model is about 16.9 megabytes, runs on CPU with no dependencies, and does not require a GPU.
The 16.9 megabyte transcription model handles up to 30 seconds of audio in one pass, auto-detects language, and can provide word timestamps.
The tiny transcription model is faster than Whisper Base and decodes about six times faster, with lower error rates on some benchmarks.
Phon 2 is an open-source transcription model under 900 megabytes that can turn an hour of audio into text in about 20 seconds.
Phon 2 has free Hugging Face spaces for online testing and achieves the second lowest average error rate among the compared models.
Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 5.5, which improves on the previous Sonnet for agentic coding and knowledge work tasks and scores close to Opus 5.5.
Claude Sonnet 5.5 ranks second on the Artificial Analysis intelligence index, beating GPT6 Astra, but is not necessarily cheaper to run than Opus.
claims: In Spatial World 1.5 gives users control over how a scene is viewed based on a chosen camera trajectory.
Soul Refiner is not fully faithful to the original video because it can change details while sharpening the image.
The 16.9 megabyte transcription model is the smallest transcription model the speaker has seen so far.
Phon 2 performs very well compared with much larger transcription models.
Claude Sonnet 5.5 punches well above its weight for agentic coding and knowledge work tasks.
Claude Sonnet 5.5 is not very impressive in terms of efficiency because it produces the most output tokens per task.
For best intelligence, the speaker recommends Opus or Fable, and for best performance per cost, GPT 6.1 Soul or GPT6 Astra.
quotes: AI never sleeps and this week has been absolutely insane.
Gemini 4 Argon and it's an absolute beast.
This can basically take any image plus a camera path and it'll generate a video walking in the scene through that camera path.
this is based off of one 2.1. I'm surprised they haven't used Miniax H3 for this, but anyway, this is based off of 1 1.3b.
And this is only less than 6 GB in size, so you should be able to fit this on most consumer GPUs.
Soul Refiner by Nvidia, and this takes lowresolution video and upscales it into a sharper highresolution video up to 4K in a single step.
So this is not really faithful.
This is only like 16.9 megabytes in size.
You don't even need a GPU to run this.
It also decodes like six times faster.
This is a bit larger, so it's under 900 megabytes, which is still really small compared to other TTS models that are at least gigabytes in size.
This can turn an hour of audio into text in about only 20 seconds.
takeaways: Use In Spatial World 1.5 when you need camera-path control over generated scene videos and can run a sub-6 GB model on consumer GPUs.
Use Nvidia Soul Refiner for fast single-step video upscaling, but verify important details because it can alter source content.
Use the 16.9 megabyte transcription model for lightweight, CPU-only transcription on phones or edge devices.
Use Phon 2 when you need a small open-source transcription model with strong benchmark performance and free online demos.
Treat Claude Sonnet 5.5 as a strong free-plan default, but choose Opus or Fable for maximum intelligence and GPT 6.1 Soul or GPT6 Astra for better cost efficiency.

items.title: How 168 Men Captured the Inca Emperor - Si Sheppard
summary_lines: Francisco Pizarro, distant cousin of Cortez, took the playbook from Cortez's conquest.
168 men encountered Atahualpa outside Cajamarca in 1532; Atahualpa had just won the Inca civil war and was proceeding to Cuzco to be enthroned Sapa Inca.

Pizarro sent a lieutenant to display horsemanship, the horse charged Atahualpa and stopped inches from his face, snorting; Atahualpa remained stony-faced and said "I will meet with your master at a time of my choosing."
After the Spaniards left, Atahualpa executed his own court members, including generals who flinched or showed fear, to prove he would not be intimidated.
items.why: A concise retelling of how 168 men exploited a civil-war-weakened empire, relevant as a historical parallel for asymmetric power dynamics.

deep.gist: Francisco Pizarro used a Cortes style playbook to confront Atahualpa with 168 men outside Cajamarca in 1532. After a horse display and a delayed meeting, Pizarro lured Atahualpa into a narrow courtyard and captured him with artillery and musketry. The capture is framed as seizing the top of the social hierarchy to control the whole structure.
key_points: Francisco Pizarro, called a distant cousin of Cortez, met Cortez and took a playbook for conquest.
Atahualpa had won the Inca civil war and was moving to Cuzco for formal enthronement as Sapa Inca.
168 Spanish men entered the Inca realm, and Atahualpa met them outside Cajamarca in 1532.
Atahualpa treated the Spaniards as an opportunity rather than a threat.
Pizarro sent a key lieutenant to perform a horsemanship display before the Sapa Inca.
The horse charged at Atahualpa and his court, then stopped inches from his face.
Atahualpa stayed stony-faced and said he would meet Pizarro at a time of his choosing.
Atahualpa executed court members and generals who flinched or showed fear.
Atahualpa later met Pizarro at Cajamarca with a vast army.
A Peruvian saying holds that Atahualpa planned to have Pizarro for lunch, but Pizarro had him for breakfast.
Pizarro waited until Atahualpa entered a narrow constricted courtyard before launching the ambush.
Pizarro used artillery and musketry for shock value, overwhelmed Atahualpa, and took him prisoner.
claims: Pizarro obtained a playbook from Cortez for how to carry out the capture.
Atahualpa saw the Spaniards as an opportunity rather than a threat.
Pizarro used a horse display to impress the Sapa Inca.
Atahualpa executed fearful courtiers to prevent intimidation.
Seizing the top of the social hierarchy controls the entire structure.
quotes: This is the land of the Inca.
Atahualpa had just won the civil war
seize whoever is at the very top
takeaways: A small armed force can capture a large empire's leader by exploiting terrain and shock.
Controlling the apex of a hierarchy can paralyze the whole structure.
Atahualpa's display of fearlessness and execution of fearful courtiers did not prevent capture.
Pizarro's ambush relied on luring the emperor into a confined courtyard.

items.title: How to stop AI from making you dumber
summary_lines: Cognitive offloading to Claude or ChatGPT can erode critical thinking and writing skills, but the effect is reversible if you stop using AI for a while.
For novice skills like coding, do the thinking yourself instead of outsourcing it to AI; expert skills are more durable and less susceptible to de-skilling.
Update Claude or ChatGPT instructions to say you want to learn and build skills, then ask it to ask follow-up questions or quiz you.
Exit the AI tool and read primary sources instead of sending a dozen prompts and skimming a wall of text.
Run a one- or two-week test without AI to see which skills you lost.
items.why: It gives a practical protocol to keep AI from replacing the thinking you need.
items.description:
An overreliance on AI chatbots can make you … well … dumber.   When you're using AI, you're offloading a lot more, and over time, you can see skills like critical thinking and writing get worse. Vox’s Adam Clark Estes gives three tips for getting these skills back.

takeaways: Use AI intentionally, not for tasks that require building a new skill.
Set chatbot instructions to quiz and follow up when learning.
Add friction by reading primary sources instead of consuming long AI outputs.

items.title: Why so many boys grow up to be lonely
summary_lines: Boys as young as 4 are taught stoicism and independence through phrases like «Boys don't cry», «toughen up», and «don't be a girl».
US men have shrinking friendship circles, record labor-force exit rates, and higher suicide rates than US women.
A 2017 study found young men saw self-sufficiency, toughness, hypersexuality, financial provider role, and control as cornerstones of masculinity, with pressure from family, friends, and society.
The shift from having friends to share deepest secrets to drifting away happens during teen years, by the end of high school.

Adults can counter it by saying sharing feelings and platonic connections is a universal human need, being present when boys are ready to talk, and men modeling their own disappointment, sadness, and embarrassment.
items.why: It points to early socialization as the lever for male loneliness and suicide risk.
items.description:

items.title: DIGGER EXPLAINED: WTF Is This Movie?
summary_lines: Digger is directed by Alejandro Gonzalez Inaritu and stars Tom Cruise as Curtis Markson, an actor portraying a fictionalized oil tycoon named Digger Rockwell.

The film opens with Digger Rockwell waking in a stage-like estate; his cat Maggie defecates and vomits on him while employee Sandy reports methane under permafrost in a glacier has ruptured, causing flames and a massive crack.
Advisers led by Dr. Narav Ganesh, played by Riz Aamemed, say a massive iceberg is heading toward the North Sea, threatening hundreds of millions of lives in coastal Europe.

President Thompson, played by John Goodman, and vice president Eddie, played by Michael Stolbar, debate bombing the iceberg or waiting for winds and currents to carry it south; they choose not to warn Europe.

The twist: everything up to that point is a theatrical production; Tom Cruise is actually Curtis Markson, an actor portraying a fictionalized version of real oil tycoon Digger Rockwell, whose company caused an environmental crisis and inspired a play called Fossil Fools.
items.why: It decodes a confusing meta-structure that turns a climate disaster into a staged performance.

deep.gist: Eric Boss explains Digger as a Brechtian, theatrical satire that hides its play-within-a-play structure until the middle of the film. The movie uses exaggerated performance, stage mechanics, and a climate disaster plot to comment on environmental destruction, myth-making, and the end of Warner Brothers as an independent studio.
key_points: Digger is directed by Alejandro Gonzalez Inaritu and stars Tom Cruz as Curtis Markson, an actor playing Digger Rockwell.
The opening shows oil tycoon Digger Rockwell waking in a theatrical estate while methane under permafrost ruptures.
An ice shelf breaks off and threatens coastal Europe, while President Thompson and advisers debate whether to bomb it or wait.
The film reveals that the first act is actually a theatrical production, an adaptation of a play called Fossil Fools.
The production is funded by Kenny Rockwell, the real tycoon's nephew, and directed by Hannah.
The staging uses impossible stage doors, muted costumes, makeup, and set design to create a Brechtian presentational satire.
Curtis struggles to reach his daughter during a category 6 hurricane, while Kenny offers help backstage.
The play's plot includes Rockwell feeding expensive tuna to a dying cat, then addressing European leaders and winning some over with a rotating-stage dance.
A second glacier from northern Siberia releases nuclear waste, prompting a plan to bomb the ice shelf despite warnings that each chunk becomes a radioactive bomb.
Curtis objects to historical details about Air Force One, and the cast debates whether the work is farce or satire.
Kenny argues the play exists to let audiences vent anger at his uncle and villainize the perpetrators in a broken world.
The premiere ends with Digger Rockwell drowning himself on an oil platform after Europe floods and food is gone.
After the curtain call, a level four air quality warning makes the cast wear gas masks and exit into a polluted, flooded Midtown Manhattan with drones and no birds.
The film was made on a $160 million budget, shot by Emanuel Lubeski in Vista Vision, and is framed as the last Warner Brothers film before Skydance and David Ellison ownership.
Eric Boss compares it to Mr. Burns, a post-electric play, and says it is both admirable and annoying.
claims: The film's central twist is that the apparent movie is actually a theatrical production.
Brechtian theater is used to make the audience uncomfortable and deliver political commentary.
The film is a bold art house experiment that Hollywood should support, even if it is hard to sit through.
The ending extends the polluted air warning to the real theater audience.
Digger is the last Warner Brothers film before Skydance and David Ellison ownership.
quotes: Is Digger Tom Cruz's biggest bomb or the most important film this year that comments on the way this world is changing?

The big twist of this movie, something not at all communicated in the marketing, is that everything we have seen up until this point is actually a theatrical production, a play within the play of this movie.
I admire Gonzalez initiu and Tom Cruz for making a bold art house movie like this
people would leave the theater breathless.
takeaways: Understand Digger as a Brechtian satire, not a conventional disaster film.
Notice the theatrical mechanics: impossible doors, set design, costumes, and stage movement.
The film uses myth and adaptation to comment on climate crisis and corporate responsibility.
It can be admired as a bold experiment while also being annoying.
The ending implicates the audience in the polluted world.

deep.gist: Eric Boss breaks down Jordan Peele's Get Out as a social horror film built from layered symbols, racial anxieties, and horror film references. The analysis traces the sunken place, the Armmitage household, the red alchemist society, and the film's many nods to The Shining, Rosemary's Baby, and other horror works.
key_points: Get Out is framed as a social horror film that changed modern Hollywood horror over the past decade.
The sunken place is a metaphor for marginalization and loss of control.
The stirring spoon sound connects to Chris's childhood trauma and becomes the trigger for hypnosis.
The opening suburb is a nod to John Carpenter's Halloween and to the idea that horror can happen in a perfect white neighborhood.
Andre's white-voiced phone call foreshadows the later body takeover.
The film's 1 hour 44 minute runtime comes from many drafts and tight editing.
The white car with black interior mirrors the cult's plan to put black souls into white bodies.
Jeremy's antique Templar helmet and red clothing connect to the red alchemist society mythology.
The title Get Out comes from Eddie Murphy's 1983 Delirious special.
Chris's shaving cream is read as a whiteface metaphor.
Rose's hair changes from loose to tightly pulled back as her true self emerges.
The Armmitage home uses plantation imagery, deer symbolism, and Omega symbols to signal control and false immortality.
Dean's tour maps the house like The Shining, showing where the horror will happen.
Missy's spoon stirring and unbroken eye contact hypnotize Chris into the sunken place.
The party functions as a slave auction, with bingo cards and the red alchemist society's relic trade.
claims: The sunken place is a metaphor for the marginalization of the black horror movie audience.
Get Out exposes the hypocrisy of white liberals.
American racism exists in suburbs, northern rural areas, and Hollywood, not only in the American South.
The film uses horror symbols to show how racism can operate through gaslighting and subtle control.
quotes: Sink into the floor.
Now you're in the sunken place.
It's like a hedge maze out here.
Get out. Too bad we can't stay, baby.
I don't want to get chased off the lawn with a shotgun.
My dad would have voted for Obama a third time if he could have.
Such a privilege to be able to experience another person's culture.
We had to seal it up. That's some black mold down there.
My mother loved her kitchen, so we keep a piece of her in here.
One day you're developing prince in the dark room, the next day you wake up in the dark.
ROD WAS RIGHT. GET OUT.
takeaways: Read Get Out as a social horror film, not just a thriller.
Notice how the sunken place represents loss of control and marginalization.
Track the film's horror references, especially The Shining and Rosemary's Baby.
Watch for symbols like the spoon, deer, red clothing, and the Armmitage house.
The film argues that racism can be subtle, liberal, and everywhere.

items.title: The Cure for Unrequited Love #animation #facts #fearofintimacy
summary_lines: The cure for unrequited love is not forgetting the beloved but learning to think more intensely and constructively about who they might really be
The cruelty: our hopes are aroused by someone who can never disappoint us, and we keep believing in them because we lack the knowledge that would set us free
The imaginative cure: accept, without knowing the details, that they would eventually prove decisively irritating; everyone does, because they are human
items.why: Flips the standard «just get over it» advice into a concrete cognitive move: stop idealizing, start expecting the flaws you already know every person has.
items.description:
The real cruelty of unrequited love is that we don’t get to know our beloveds well enough to find out their flaws – and therefore to lose interest in them gradually. The best cure for love is in essence: get to know them better.  

Enjoying our Youtube videos? Get full access to all our audio content, videos, and thousands of thought-provoking articles, conversation cards and more with The School of Life Subscription: https://t.ly/iWdtx

Be more mindful, present and inspired. Get the best of The School of Life delivered straight to your inbox: https://t.ly/P6FFo

FURTHER READING

“For intense periods of our lives, we suffer the agony of unrequited love. Our sorrow is accompanied by a certainty that if only the elusive being would return our smiles, come for dinner or marry us, we would know bliss. Epochal happiness seems tantalisingly close, wholly real and yet maddeningly out of reach. At such moments, we are often counselled to try to forget the beloved. We should – given their lack of interest – try to think of something or someone else. Yet this kindness is deeply misguided. The cure for love does not lie in ceasing to think of the fugitive lover, but in learning to think more intensely and constructively about who they might really be…”

items.title: Inside the ML4Good Technical AI Safety Bootcamp: What to Expect
summary_lines: ML4Good is an eight-day technical AI safety bootcamp near Lyon, France, covering AI agents, alignment, model reasoning, evaluations, interpretability, and AI governance
The bootcamp is completely free: accommodation and three meals per day provided, plus transportation reimbursement up to 180 euros
The interview runs 10-15 minutes with five sequential questions, 2-3 minutes to answer each; results arrive within a couple of days
Application questions include «Why are you applying for this programme?» and «What are your thoughts on the risks and benefits of AI?»
items.why: A free, fully-catered eight-day technical bootcamp with a short structured interview is a low-cost on-ramp into the AI safety research community.
items.description:
TL;DR
i) ML4Good is an intensive eight-day technical AI safety bootcamp covering topics such as AI agents, alignment, model reasoning, evaluations, interpretability, and AI governance.

ii) It provides useful information about fellowships, career opportunities, starting an AI safety startup, and the broader AI safety ecosystem.

iii) I would encourage people interested in AI safety to apply, including those who already have a solid technical background.

Introduction

Hello world!

I want to share the experience I gained from the ML4Good bootcamp in technical AI safety, held near Lyon, France. In this blog post, I will try to summarize everything in short, from the application and interview process to the bootcamp experience itself.

Application Process

So, let us start with the application process. It is quite simple: go to the official ML4Good website and apply for the cohort you would like to join. See the section “Find a Bootcamp”. The application itself is straightforward. You have to complete a form where you are asked to answer questions ranging from “Why are you applying for this programme?” to “What are your thoughts on the risks and benefits of AI?”

After submitting the application, you have to wait for some time to see whether you pass the pre-selection stage. If you do, you will receive an email saying that you have proceeded to the next phase, together with a calendar where you can choose the most suitable date and time for an interview with a human (non-AI interview 😂). After the interview, you can expect to receive the results within a couple of days.

Interview Process

Now, let’s jump to the interview itself. I am not allowed to post the exact questions I was asked. The interview is brief, lasting around 10–15 minutes. You are asked five questions sequentially, and you have around 2–3 minutes to answer each one.

If you receive a positive email after the interview, CONGRATS you are in! The adventure can begin. The organizers will send you an email asking you to confirm your participation, together with some general questions regarding food, for example whether you have any allergies or dietary restrictions.

If you are not selected, do not get discouraged and apply for the future cohorts!

Costs and Accommodation

It is also worth mentioning that this bootcamp is completely FREE! They provide accommodation and three meals per day. Amazing, right?

You can also request reimbursement for transportation costs of up to 180€. So, depending on your travel expenses, the bootcamp can cover almost all of your costs.
 

Bootcamp Experience

Cross-posted from Substack.

Below, I’ve included 5 recommendations for hiring managers in AI Safety and 5 tips for candidates as they navigate their career search. I’ve also highlighted orgs I think are doing hiring particularly well (from a candidate’s perspective) and strategies to avoid.

Note for Readers: I do not have a technical background, and have never applied to technical roles. Therefore the reflections below are more applicable to generalist, operations, convenings, grantmaking, policy, and field-building roles in AI Safety. As orgs scale, their processes may change rapidly. These insights are locked in time from the 2026 hiring cycle.

5 Tips For Candidates:

  1. Every interview is a data point that helps you understand where your expertise fits into the ecosystem and where you can have the most impact. The hiring process is not a personal rejection or reflection of you, your talent, or the knowledge you bring to the field. Some roles I applied to were closed without ever hiring anyone.
  2. After taking the BlueDot Impact courses and adding that experience to my resume, my percentage of applications to interview invitations went way up. If you’re making a career pivot and you don’t have previous experience at an AI Safety org or frontier lab, hiring managers are looking for indicators that you've taken steps to actively be part of the AI Safety community, upskill, and continue your education. See my previous post on Comparing AI Policy Courses.
  3. I was skeptical when it launched, but I am actually very impressed by the 80,000 Hours AI Career Advisor. Their LLM can tailor your resume, edit your cover letter and application questions, run mock interviews, and provide feedback on work test submissions. Start here before applying for a personal 1-1 advising session with Probably Good, SuccessIf, or 80,000 Hours (which are more competitive and often have long waiting periods).
  4. Many smaller AI Safety orgs work with third-party providers like Impact Ops and Mangr

items.title: Reducing synthetic markers makes some SDF false facts linearly indistinguishable from pretraining-acquired knowledge
summary_lines: Synthetic Document Finetuning (SDF), the state-of-the-art method for implanting false beliefs into LLMs, produces training documents with detectable synthetic markers that make implanted facts distinguishable from pretraining knowledge via middle-layer linear probes

Reducing those markers lets SDF implant subtly-implausible false facts that a middle-layer linear probe cannot distinguish from genuine pretraining knowledge; applying RPO afterward strengthens the false facts monotonically, though overtraining remains detectable

Egregiously-implausible false facts stay detectable even after marker reduction, and even when internal representations match pretraining knowledge, false facts do not always propagate to downstream reasoning tasks

The motivation: a sufficiently intelligent model could inspect its own beliefs and flag oddly-represented ones as implanted, undermining the utility of false-fact implants for alignment evaluation or AI control
items.why: Shows a concrete path to making implanted false beliefs representationally invisible to linear probes, which changes the threat model for AI control and alignment evaluation.

items.title: MATS × CG Pitch Week: What Happened, What We Learned
summary_lines: The first MATS x Coefficient Giving Pitch Week (Q2 2026, four weeks, joint with Constellation and Catalyze Impact) drew 38 expressions of interest, 17 team applications, and 15 pitches
$4.3M was awarded across six grants (47% of pitching teams): five org-founding grants and two independent research grants

Funding outcomes were not strongly correlated with observable founder characteristics; what distinguished winners was idea maturity: a named first user, a concrete first deliverable, bounded scope, evidence of technical feasibility, and a legible reason the work required a new organization

MATS alumni-founded orgs Apollo and Timaeus are cited as likely accounting for an outsized share of MATS impact; new MATS Founding and Field-Building track, GovAI EIR, and Generator Residency are named as founder-support exceptions
items.why: $4.3M in six grants from a single four-week pitch program, with a clear taxonomy of what separates funded from unfunded pitches, is a useful template for anyone trying to launch an AI safety org.
items.description:
TL;DR

In Q2 2026, we ran the first MATS x Coefficient Giving (CG) Pitch Week: a four-week program designed to take fellowship researchers from an early idea to a funding decision. The program was a joint effort between MATS, CG, Constellation, and Catalyze Impact.

  • 38 expressions of interest; all were invited to a two-week Exploration Sprint. 17 teams applied and 15 teams pitched.
  • $4.3M was awarded across six grants (47% of teams that pitched) with five org-founding grants and two independent research grants.
  • Funding outcomes were not strongly correlated with the founder characteristics we could observe. What distinguished successful pitches was the maturity and evaluability of the idea: a named first user, a concrete first deliverable, a bounded scope, evidence of technical feasibility, and a legible reason the work required a new organization.

Why we ran this, and why we're writing it up

We believe that supporting founders could be unusually valuable. AI safety orgs founded by MATS alumni, such as Apollo and Timaeus, likely account for an outsized share of MATS’s impact. New organizations can also act as capacity multipliers, especially now that funding is outstripping the supply of organizations ready to absorb it, making founder support one of our highest-leverage activities.

At the same time, AI safety needs more people who can work independently, set strategy, manage teams, and build organizations. It remains an open question whether the field is short of such people or short of the infrastructure to help technically strong researchers make the transition. Talent programs such as MATS primarily select and train for research ability, not for founder-specific skills and experience. (Note: the new MATS Founding & Field-Building track, the GovAI Entrepreneur-in-Residence, and the Generator Residency are exceptions.)

items.title: High p(doom) but relaxed working
summary_lines: When presenting high p(doom) to non-AI safety or transitioning personnel, avoid portraying high values without sharing counterarguments and point them toward emotional support.
An Evan Hub tweet from the Alignment Science lead at Anthropic claims a >10% chance all humans will be killed by AI, shared in response to a pre-training researcher resigning due to safety concerns.
Repeatedly presenting catastrophic outcomes without emotional support or time to process is only partially helpful for attracting and retaining talent in the field.

The author agrees with Spencer Greenberg's 80000hours podcast on existential risk mental health 12 levers, specifically finding a productive version of yourself without constant hypervigilance and anxiety.
items.why: Unmitigated doom messaging actively hurts retention and onboarding of new talent in the field.
items.description:
tl;dr

  1. If you are working in AI safety, while presenting information to interested non-AI safety or transitioning personnel, avoid portraying high values of p(doom) without sharing counterarguments. In addition, please give them time and point them towards emotional support so the unprecedented risk can be processed at their own pace.
  2. Encourage those transitioning and working in the field to find ways to deal with said p(doom) looming over their heads on a day-to-day basis. This work will most likely require exploration and lead to highly individual outcomes.
  3. Share and celebrate progress in the field! Managing one's own motivation is difficult work and reminding each other that achievements/progress are being made can be helpful.

Intro

I have found myself overwhelmed when thinking about existential risk. Joking with peers about it provided necessary momentary distraction. Usually, after a moment of relief, discussions and work could continue more productively. I would like to make the case that repeatedly presenting catastrophic outcomes without emotional support and/or time to process is only partially helpful, both for attracting and retaining talent in the field.

My aim in this post is to verbalise my impressions around how existential risk, its urgency and the sensation of "doom" in particular are presented and circulated within the field. If you consider yourself ASI-pilled, the below perspective could seem outright wrong. In that case, please help me understand your viewpoint without getting overwhelmed by a sense of hopelessness.

Basis

I assume that many readers here will have engaged with the podcast with Spencer Greenberg. I think it is a very good baseline and find myself agreeing with his statements and recommendations, in particular about finding a version of yourself that is productive without being in a constant state of hypervigilance and anxiety.

However, in my opinion, how existential risk is being communicated and processed adds an additional strain that goes beyond general career advice, like finding engaging work, and frameworks like positive vs. negative stress.

items.title: Will ₹1 Crore Still Be Worth ₹1 Crore in 20 Years?
summary_lines: At 6% annual inflation, a ₹1 lakh item costs roughly ₹3.2 lakh in 20 years; ₹1 crore in nominal terms shrinks to about ₹31 lakh in today's purchasing power.
The short frames financial planning as two questions: how much money you need, and what that money will actually be worth in the future.
The transcript field contains only a YouTube-transcript.ai API promotion, not the video's audio; all figures come from the description.
items.why: The 6% compounding math shows why a fixed ₹1 crore savings target silently loses two-thirds of its buying power over two decades.
items.description:
₹1 crore sounds like a lot of money today, but what will it actually be worth 20 years from now?

If inflation averages 6% per year, prices keep rising over time and the purchasing power of your money declines.
For example, something that costs ₹1 lakh today could cost around ₹3.2 lakh in 20 years at 6% annual inflation.

So, while your ₹1 crore remains ₹1 crore in nominal terms, its purchasing power could be equivalent to only around ₹31 lakh in today's money after 20 years.
That’s why financial planning isn't just about asking:
“How much money will I need?
It’s also about asking:
"How much will that money actually be worth in the future?"

#Inflation #PersonalFinance #Investing #FinancialPlanning #Money #₹1Crore #PurchasingPower #Finance

Buffett is cited as taking a salary for living expenses while building wealth through stock.

build, build, build, borrow, die.

items.title: How to change the world: what 24 years of campaigning taught us
summary_lines: Richard Murphy and John Christensen co-founded the Tax Justice Network 24 years ago, when it was the only organization dedicated to campaigning on tax justice issues.
They met at the Royal Yacht Hotel in St. Helia, Jersey, and Christensen had been working with Professor Prem Sika, Lord Sika, on tax justice matters.
The podcast’s core claim is that problems without solutions breed despair, so campaigning must describe a better future and build credible proposals to reach it.
The description says their 2002 Jersey work began developing country-by-country reporting, which later contributed to major changes in international tax transparency.
items.why: It offers a concrete campaign playbook: imagine the outcome, build workable policy, understand opponents, and persist.
items.description:
How do you actually change the world?

In this Funding the Future podcast, I talk with my old friend and fellow Tax Justice Network co-founder John Christensen about what 24 years of campaigning have taught us.

Our argument is simple: problems without solutions breed despair.

Campaigning cannot just identify what is wrong, explain who is responsible or make people angry. Successful campaigning has to describe what a better future might look like and then develop credible proposals for getting there.

John and I discuss how this approach shaped our work on tax justice. When we first met in Jersey in 2002, we began developing what became country-by-country reporting. That campaign eventually contributed to major changes in international tax transparency.

We discuss what we learned from that experience: imagine the outcome you want; develop workable policies; understand your opponents’ arguments; build networks; create a story people can understand; engage with political power; and have the persistence to keep going.

We also consider how solution-focused campaigning could be applied to today’s problems, from social care and the NHS to inequality and climate change.

For decades we have been told that there is no alternative.

There are always alternatives.

The challenge is to imagine them, make them credible and build the support needed to make them happen.

items.title: What is money, really?
summary_lines: Money is described as a system for recording promises and debts, not a physical thing; banknotes, coins, and account balances are representations of obligations.
When a bank makes a loan, it records the borrower’s debt and creates a spendable deposit; when the loan is repaid, those records are cancelled and the created money disappears.
Government spending creates money, while taxation removes it; the requirement to settle taxes in pounds creates continuing demand for sterling.
Money must not be confused with real wealth, because money cannot build houses, grow food, teach children, or care for people.
items.why: It reframes money as accounting for obligations, which changes how one thinks about lending, taxes, and economic capacity.
items.description:
What is money? We use it every day, but most of what we are taught about money misrepresents what it actually is. In this Understanding Economics video, I explain why money is not a physical thing at all.

Banknotes, coins and the numbers in your bank account are representations of something else, which are promises to pay. Money records debts between people, banks and governments. What you think of as money in your bank account is, in accounting terms, just a promise made to you by your bank.

This is not a new idea. From tally sticks and coins to banknotes and modern electronic payments, money has always depended upon records of obligations. When payments take place today, nothing physical has to move between bank accounts. Accounting records simply change to show who owes what to whom.

Banks also create new money when they lend. When a bank provides a loan, it simultaneously records the borrower’s debt and creates a deposit that can be spent. When that loan is repaid, those records are cancelled, and that means that the money the loan created then disappears.

Government money works through a similar process. Government spending creates money, while taxation removes it. The requirement to settle taxes in pounds also creates continuing demand for sterling throughout the UK economy.

But, in all this, money should never be confused with real wealth. Money cannot build houses, grow food, teach children or care for people. Those things require people, skills, knowledge and physical resources.

Money is an extraordinarily important economic tool, but it is ultimately a system for recording promises and organising economic activity. Understanding that distinction between money and real wealth is fundamental to understanding how our economy actually works.

items.title: What if fiscal headroom doesn't exist?
summary_lines: Fiscal headroom is not a pot of money at the Bank of England; it is the estimated margin by which the government is forecast to meet the fiscal rules it chose to impose on itself.

Changing the fiscal rule, the economic forecast, or assumptions about growth, tax receipts, spending, or interest rates can make billions of pounds of headroom appear or vanish without anything changing in the real economy.

Murphy argues the UK's real constraints are people, skills, infrastructure, and energy, not numbers on Treasury spreadsheets, and that policy should be judged by employment, investment, public services, inflation, sustainability, and well-being.
The video is timed to the UK Budget 2026, where the phrase «fiscal headroom» is repeated by politicians, economists, and journalists as though it were a fixed constraint.
items.why: The Budget 2026 debate is being framed around a number that shifts with every assumption change, and this video gives a concrete alternative framing for the real constraints on public spending.
items.description:
As the UK approaches the Budget, one phrase is going to be repeated again and again is “fiscal headroom”. Politicians, economists and journalists talk about it as though it represents money the Chancellor has available to spend. In this video, I argue that this is deeply misleading.

Fiscal headroom is not a pot of money sitting at the Bank of England. It is simply the estimated margin by which the government is forecast to meet the fiscal rules it has chosen to impose upon itself.

Those rules are political choices. Change the fiscal rule, change the economic forecast, or change assumptions about growth, tax receipts, spending or interest rates, and billions of pounds of supposed fiscal headroom can appear or disappear without anything changing in the real economy.

I argue that this focus on fiscal headroom distracts us from the questions that really matter. The UK’s economic constraints are not numbers on Treasury spreadsheets, but the people, skills, infrastructure, energy and other resources available to meet society’s needs.

Instead of asking whether there is enough fiscal headroom for investment, pensions, healthcare, education or tackling poverty, we should ask whether the economy has the capacity to provide them and how that capacity can be expanded.

Economic policy should be judged by employment, investment, public services, inflation, sustainability and people’s well-being, not by the margin between a self-imposed fiscal rule and an uncertain economic forecast.

Fiscal headroom does not tell us what government can afford. I argue that it turns political choices into supposed accounting necessities, and that leads to bad economics and bad political decisions.

items.title: Interest rates: what are you really paying for?
summary_lines: Commercial banks create new money through accounting records when they lend; they do not need to collect deposits first, and the creation process costs very little.
Murphy argues interest should be split into three transparent charges: a basic charge for using money, an administrative charge, and a separate premium for genuine credit risk.
He is not arguing for abolishing interest; he argues the basic rate on low-risk money should be close to zero in real terms, with genuine costs and risks identified and charged separately.
Higher interest rates redistribute income toward financial-wealth owners and raise mortgages, rents, and borrowing costs, while discouraging productive investment and green-transition spending.
items.why: The video reframes interest from a natural market force into a bundle of charges that can be separated, which changes who pays what and who profits from borrowing.
items.description:
Why should money earn interest simply because somebody owns it? We usually treat interest as a natural and inevitable part of the economy, but in this Understanding Economics video, I question whether that assumption is justified.

Commercial banks do not need to collect deposits before making loans. When a bank lends, it creates new money through its accounting records. The process of creating that money itself costs very little, so why are interest rates often so high, even after allowing for the fact that lending does involve administration and the risk that borrowers will not repay?

That question is especially appropriate when much lending is now virtually risk-free. Interest should not be confused with an investment return. Investment involves taking a genuine risk in the hope of making a profit. Interest, by contrast, is a payment for allowing somebody else to use money for a period of time.

I argue that we should separate the different costs currently bundled together as interest. Borrowers could instead see a basic charge for using money, an administrative charge and a separate premium reflecting the genuine credit risk involved.

This matters because interest rates have significant economic consequences. Higher rates redistribute income towards people who own financial wealth while increasing mortgages, rents and borrowing costs. They can also discourage productive investment and spending on priorities such as the green transition.

I am not arguing that interest should be abolished. I am arguing that the basic interest rate on low-risk money should be close to zero in real terms, while genuine costs and risks should be identified and charged transparently.

Understanding what we are actually paying for would make borrowing clearer, improve competition and help us understand who gains and who loses from the interest rates that shape our economy.

items.title: A Case for Tool Libraries
summary_lines: A study of roughly 5,000 respondents across two regions found the average drill gets used 8 minutes per year.

The short is an excerpt from a full episode with Pieter de Beer, linked at realprogressives.org.

The average drill gets used 8 minutes a year. We don't need 8 billion drills, only a few to serve the community. 
Coordination is where working class power lives.
Link to full ep ft Pieter de Beer: https://realprogressives.org/mnc-podcast-ep/episode-399-resistance-and-resilience-with-pieter-de-beer/

#community #coordination #WorkingClass

summary_lines: Bill Gates, yapay zekânın kötü niyetli kişilerin elinde siber saldırı, dolandırıcılık, kritik altyapı hedef alması ve biyolojik güvenlik riskleri kapsayan küresel bir tehdide dönüşebileceği uyarısında bulundu.

items.why: AI kontrol krizi ve veri güvenliği, küresel teknoloji yarışının merkezine oturdu; Türkiye'nin de etkileneceği konularda erken uyanış lazım.
items.description:
Bill Gates, yapay zekânın kötü niyetli kişilerin elinde büyük bir küresel tehdide dönüşebileceği uyarısında bulunuyor. Siber saldırılardan dolandırıcılığa, kritik altyapıların hedef alınmasından biyolojik güvenlik risklerine kadar uzanan tehlikelere dikkat çeken Gates, teknoloji şirketlerinin kendi kendini denetlemesinin yeterli olmadığını, devletlerin de düzenleme süreçlerine dahil olması gerektiğini savunuyor.

Öte yandan ABD ile Çin arasındaki yapay zekâ rekabetinde yeni bir tartışma gündemde. OpenAI, Çinli Moonshot AI ile bağlantılı kullanıcıları modellerinden gizli bilgiler elde etmeye çalışmakla suçladı. Şirketin açıklamasına göre, 24-25 Temmuz tarihlerinde 4 binden fazla kullanıcıdan 16 bin istek geldi.
Yapay zekâ yarışı artık yalnızca teknolojik üstünlükten ibaret değil. Veri güvenliği, fikri mülkiyet ve teknolojinin kontrolü de küresel rekabetin merkezine yerleşiyor.

Peki yapay zekâ çağında asıl güç, en gelişmiş modeli üretmek mi, yoksa onu kontrol edebilmek mi?

items.title: Komünist Bakış | Fon soygununda konuşulmayanlar
summary_lines: TKP General Secretary Kemal Okuyan argues the Fon robbery debate wrongly separates 'normal' robbery from the system itself being a robbery mechanism, financial markets extract surplus value ('artı değer sömürüsü') with zero production and zero value addition.

deep.gist: Irem Yildirim interviews Kemal Okuyan, general secretary of the Communist Party of Turkey, about the Turkish fund and stock-market scandal. Okuyan argues that the immediate theft is a criminal case, but the deeper problem is that financial markets are a legal mechanism for transferring wealth from ordinary people to capital. He says the state, AKP, regulators, and powerful market actors are implicated, and that compensation for victims is necessary but not enough without challenging the market mechanism itself.
key_points: Okuyan separates the scandal into two layers: a specific criminal theft and a broader system in which financial markets transfer wealth from citizens to capital.
He says financial markets do not create production value and function like a legal gambling system in which small investors lose on average.
He compares legal betting to the stock market, saying that in betting roughly 80 percent of the money returns to players and 20 percent goes to betting companies and intermediaries.
He gives a simplified example: put in 10 lira, get back 8 lira, and lose 2 lira on average per transaction.
He says the modern stock exchange emerged in the early 17th century in Amsterdam around a spice-trade company and historically transferred wealth from many participants to a small minority.
He says the Turkish scandal resembles the crude financial abuses of the 1920s, not the more sophisticated later manipulations seen on Wall Street.
He says about 450,000 small investors are mentioned in connection with the scandal, though it is unclear whether all of them were truly small investors.
He says at least 89 names were identified by internet watchers as having reported the emerging bubble in detail.

He says a precautionary measure was imposed on a major Turkish insurance company with a large public shareholding and then removed, which he calls an absurd error showing panic and lack of preparation.
He says AKP lost credibility from the scandal and that the system did not prove it can renew or clean itself.
He says large investors did not suffer much, while ordinary citizens who made small investments to protect savings from inflation were heavily harmed.
He says compensation for victims is necessary, but the mechanism that enabled the theft must also be challenged.
He says the state should not be expected to pay compensation from the treasury, but could use funds from institutions under precautionary measures.
He says the distinction between small investors and other participants is complex and will be used to delay and narrow compensation.
He says the only real function of the financial market in Turkey is resource transfer, which he describes as a tax-like extraction usually taken from the poor.
claims: Financial markets are a legal wealth-transfer mechanism that takes from small investors and gives to capital.
The Turkish fund scandal is not only a criminal case but also evidence of a systemic theft mechanism.
The state and AKP bear major responsibility for the scandal because they promoted financial markets and failed to prevent the manipulation.
No clean financial market exists because the underlying mechanism is inherently a transfer of wealth without production.
The scandal shows that the system lacks the claimed regulatory capacity to prevent manipulation and speculation.
The removal of a precautionary measure from a major public-shareholding insurance company shows panic and lack of preparation.
AKP suffered a credibility loss from the scandal and cannot easily turn it into a political advantage.
Compensation for victims is necessary, but it will be delayed, narrowed, and complicated by the difficulty of defining who is a small investor.
The financial market in Turkey functions like a tax taken mainly from the poor, with no productive contribution to the economy.
The fact that recorded cash flows have not raised the share of tax revenue in gross national income is a sign that the system is not working as claimed.
quotes: 10 lira koyarsan 2 lira kaybediyorsun.
10 lira verip 8 lira alıyorsun.
Temiz borsa beklemesin. Yok böyle bir şey hayatta yok.
Temiz kumar olur mu?
Bu piyasa finans piyasası tuzak. Ey yurttaşlar girmeyin bu işlere demiyorlar.
Saptadığımız en az 89 isim ayrıntı vererek buradaki ortaya çıkan balonu ihbar etmişler zaten.
Bu soygun bütün boyutlarıyla ortaya çıkmalıdır.
takeaways: The scandal should be understood as both a criminal theft and a symptom of a financial system that transfers wealth from ordinary people to capital.
Regulators and the state are not neutral referees; they promoted the market and failed to stop the manipulation.
Victim compensation is necessary, but it will likely be delayed and limited by the complexity of defining small investors.
The removal of a precautionary measure from a major insurance company is evidence of institutional panic and weak preparation.
The financial market in Turkey should be treated as a wealth-transfer mechanism, not as a neutral engine of economic growth.

items.title: Osmaniye Ve Adana'da Peş Peşe 3 Deprem
summary_lines: Kocaeli Univ. Prof. Dr. Şerif Barış called the quakes aftershocks of the Feb 6 Kahramanmaraş-Elbistan earthquake.
Standard buildings not expected to suffer destructive impact, but adobe and masonry structures warned about.
Region described as still under significant stress from the 2023 event.
items.why: Expert assessment links the sequence to the 2023 mainshock and gives a damage outlook.
items.description:
Habertürk ekranlarında son dakika gelişmesi: Adana'nın Saimbeyli ve Osmaniye'nin Sumbas ilçelerinde kısa süre içinde peş peşe üç deprem meydana geldi. Adana'da 17 dakika arayla 4.8 ve 4.9, ardından Osmaniye'de 5.2 büyüklüğünde kaydedilen sarsıntılar bölgede büyük paniğe neden oldu.

Kocaeli Üniversitesi Jeofizik Bölümü Öğretim Üyesi Prof. Dr. Şerif Barış, Habertürk canlı yayınında yaşanan hareketliliği değerlendirdi. Prof. Dr. Barış, bu sarsıntıların 6 Şubat Kahramanmaraş-Elbistan depreminin yarattığı gerilimin bir sonucu olarak ortaya çıkan artçı depremler olabileceğine dikkat çekti. 5.2 büyüklüğündeki sarsıntının standart yapılarda yıkıcı bir etki yaratmasının beklenmediğini belirten uzman isim, kerpiç ve yığma yapılara karşı vatandaşları uyardı. summary_lines: Pakistan FM Ishaq: 6+ countries want to join; names circulating: Qatar, Kuwait, Egypt, Azerbaijan, Syria.

Iran's role debated, Pezeşkiyan's pro-Islam cooperation statement seen as soft signal; Husis (Shia Zeydi group) discussed as Iran-linked.
items.why: First concrete list of prospective members and the NATO analogy for the Riyadh pact.
items.description:
Riyad'da gerçekleştirilen Mekke İttifakı toplantısının perde arkası ve bölge güvenliğine etkileri Habertürk ekranlarında değerlendiriliyor. Doç. Dr. Gökhan Çınkara ve Prof. Dr. Umut Uzer'in konuk olduğu programda, ittifaka katılmak isteyen aralarında Mısır, Katar, Suriye, Azerbaycan ve Kuveyt'in de bulunduğu 6 yeni ülkenin durumu analiz ediliyor. İttifakın NATO benzeri bir kolektif güvenlik yapısına dönüşmesi, Suudi Arabistan'ı hedef alan Husi tehdidi ve İran Cumhurbaşkanı Pezeşkiyan'ın bu oluşuma karşı açıklamaları detaylandırılıyor. Ayrıca Pakistan ordusunun bölgedeki askeri varlığı, ABD ve Avrupa ülkelerinin istihbarat desteği ve Türkiye'nin ittifaktaki stratejik rolü masaya yatırılıyor.

items.description:
#istanbultiyatrofestivali #handanuzaldündar

37 yıllık köklü tarihiyle bu yıl 30'uncu edisyonunu gerçekleştiren İstanbul Tiyatro Festivali, 22 Ekim-3 Aralık tarihleri arasında tiyatroseverlerle buluşacak. items.title: Emekliler Meydanları Doldurdu, İktidara Tepki Gösterdi! "Emekliler Sadaka Topluluğu Değildir"
summary_lines: Retired police officer Ali Şekeroğlu died by suicide in front of the Constitutional Court in Ankara while retirees protested for salary adjustments and a humane life.
His sign read «not for money, but for our dignity», and his posts included «No one can question our love for the homeland» and «they also cannot punish us with hunger».

Tüm Emeklilerin Sendikası Ankara branches said on Sakarya Caddesi: «Emekliye insanca yaşam ücreti vermek enflasyon değil, adalet meselesidir. Enflasyon bahanesiyle emekliyi açlığa mahkûm edenlerin derdi ekonomi değil, iktidarını korumaktır».
Chants included «A budget for retirees, not for the palace» and «We are retirees, we are right, we will win»; the union called the claim that pension raises raise inflation dirty propaganda.
items.why: The protest ties a retiree suicide to pension policy and frames the government's inflation argument as political cover.

items.title: Adana ve Osmaniye'de peş peşe depremler
summary_lines: Adana Saimbeyli'de saat 14.19'da 4.8 büyüklüğünde deprem (derinlik 7.99 km), saat 14.36'da 4.9 büyüklüğünde deprem (derinlik 8.67 km) oldu.
Osmaniye Sumbas'ta saat 14.43'te 5.2 büyüklüğünde deprem (derinlik 7 km) meydana geldi.
Adana Valisi Mustafa Yavuz, 112 Acil Çağrı Merkezine olumsuz ihbar alınmadığını söyledi.
Çevre Bakanı Murat Kurum, şu ana kadar olumsuz durum bildirilmediğini açıkladı.
items.why: Three earthquakes in quick succession across two provinces with no reported casualties, ongoing risk assessment.
items.description:
Haber Merkezi

Adana'nın Saimbeyli ilçesinde dakikalar arayla meydana gelen 4,8 ve 4,9 büyüklüğündeki depremlerin hemen ardından Osmaniye'nin Sumbas ilçesi de 5,2 bir deprem gerçekleşti. Yetkililer şu ana kadar herhangi bir yıkım veya can kaybı ihbarı alınmadığını duyurdu.

Adana'nın Saimbeyli ilçesinde 4,8 ve 4,9 büyüklüğünde depremler meydana geldi.

Afet ve Acil Durum Yönetimi Başkanlığının (AFAD) internet sitesinde yer alan bilgiye göre, saat 14.19'da merkez üssü Saimbeyli olan 4,8 büyüklüğünde sarsıntı kaydedildi. Depremin yerin 7,99 kilometre derinliğinde meydana geldiği belirlendi.

İlçede saat 14.36'da 4,9 büyüklüğünde bir deprem daha meydana geldi. İkinci sarsıntının yerin 8,67 kilometre derinliğinde meydana geldiği tespit edildi.

Adana Valisi Mustafa Yavuz, AA muhabirine kentte iki depremin ardından ekiplerin görevlendirildiğini söyledi. Olumsuz ihbar almadıklarını belirten Yavuz, "Şu ana kadar 112 Acil Çağrı Merkezine gelen olumsuz ihbar yok. Ekiplerimiz saha taramalarını sürdürüyor. Vatandaşlarımıza 'geçmiş olsun' diliyorum" diye konuştu. 

 Desteklemek, güç vermek için tüm okurlarımızı soL Haber'e abone olmaya davet ediyoruz.

ABONE OL

Kısa süre sonra bir deprem de Osmaniye'de meydana geldi

Kısa bir süre sonra Adana'nın komşusu Osmaniye'de de bir deprem meydana geldi.

Osmaniye'nin Sumbas ilçesinde saat 14.43'te 5,2 büyüklüğünde sarsıntı kaydedildi.

AFAD'ın internet sitesinde yer alan bilgiye göre, deprem yerin 7 kilometre derinliğinde meydana geldi.

Osmaniye Valisi Mehmet Fatih Serdengeçti tarafıdan yapılan yazılı açıklamada, "İlimizde hissedilen deprem sonrası ilgili kurumlarımızla ivedilikle koordinasyon sağlanmış olup, şu an itibarıyla herhangi bir olumsuzluk bulunmamaktadır. Yüce Mevla milletimizi her türlü afetten korusun." ifadelerine yer verildi.

Bakan Kurum: Şu ana kadar olumsuz bir durum bildirilmedi

Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği Bakanı Murat Kurum, Adana ve Osmaniye'de meydana gelen depremlerin ardından şu ana kadar olumsuz bir durum bildirilmediğini, tüm ihbarları değerlendirdiklerini bildirdi.

Bakan Kurum, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamada, şunları kaydetti:

"Adana ve Osmaniye'de meydana gelen depremlerin ardından gelişmeleri yakından takip ediyoruz. Şu ana kadar olumsuz bir durum bildirilmemekle beraber tüm ihbarları değerlendiriyoruz. Bölgedeki vatandaşlarımıza geçmiş olsun dileklerimi iletiyorum."

items.title: İspanya'da konut krizi büyüyor
summary_lines: İspanya Meclisi'nde kiracı koruma kararname 172-178 ve 166-184 oylarla reddedildi.
3 Ekim'de yaklaşık 50 kente yayılan eylemlerde Madrid'de hüküm göre 70 bin kişi yürüdü.
Birinci kararname 2030'a kadar koruma uzatmayı, kira artışlarını sınırlandırmayı, sezonluk kiralamaları düzenlemeyi içeriyordu.
İkinci kararname ev sahibinin sözleşmeyi yenilememesi halinde tazminat yükümlülüğü getiriyordu.
items.why: Parlamento reddetmesiyle sokağa taşan konut krizi, İspanya'da genel grev çağrısı gündemde.
items.description:
Dış Haberler

İspanya’da büyüyen konut krizine karşı öfke sokağa taşarken, hükümetin kiracıları korumaya dönük iki düzenlemesi Meclis’te reddedildi. 3 Ekim’de 50 kentte düzenlenen eylemlerde on binlerce kişi sokaklara çıkarken, Madrid’deki konut kampı büyümeye devam ediyor. Kiracı örgütleri genel grev çağrısını gündeme taşıdı.

İspanya’da konut krizi, hükümet ile muhalefet arasındaki parlamento hesaplaşmasının ötesine geçerek yeniden sokağın ana gündemlerinden biri haline geldi.

Başkent Madrid’de günlerdir sürdürülen konut kampının ardından 3 Ekim Cumartesi günü ülkenin yaklaşık 50 kentinde eylemler düzenlendi. Madrid’de hükümet yetkililerinin verdiği rakama göre yaklaşık 70 bin kişi yürürken, konut hakkı örgütleri katılımın çok daha yüksek olduğunu savundu. Eylemlerde kira artışlarına, tahliyelere ve konutun yatırım aracına dönüştürülmesine tepki gösterildi.

Gösterilerin hemen öncesinde ise hükümetin konut krizine ilişkin iki düzenlemesi İspanya Meclisi'nde reddedilmişti.

 Desteklemek, güç vermek için tüm okurlarımızı soL Haber'e abone olmaya davet ediyoruz.

ABONE OL

Kiracıları koruyan düzenlemeler Meclis’ten dönmüş oldu

Başbakan Pedro Sánchez hükümetinin 29 Eylül’de kabul ettiği iki kararname, artan kira bedelleri ve tahliyeler karşısında kiracıların korunmasını güçlendirmeyi amaçlıyordu.

İlk kararname 2 Ekim’de 172 kabul oyuna karşı 178 oyla reddedildi. Düzenlemeye Halk Partisi (PP), aşırı sağcı Vox, Katalan sağcı bağımsızlık yanlısı Junts ve UPN karşı çıktı. İkinci kararname ise 166 kabul oyuna karşı 184 oyla reddedildi.

İlk düzenleme, kırılgan durumdaki kiracıların alternatif konut sağlanmadan tahliye edilmesine karşı korumanın 2030 sonuna kadar uzatılmasını, mevcut kira sözleşmelerindeki artışların sınırlandırılmasını, sezonluk ve oda kiralamalarına yönelik düzenlemeleri ve spekülatif alımlara karşı bazı sınırlamaları içeriyordu. Ayrıca bazı kira sözleşmelerinin uzatılması ve uygun fiyatlı konut arzının artırılması için çeşitli mekanizmalar öngörülüyordu.

İkinci düzenleme ise kira sözleşmelerinin yenilenmesi konusunda kiracı lehine daha güçlü güvenceler getiriyordu. Ev sahibinin sözleşmeyi yenilememesi durumunda gerekçe gösterme ve belirli koşullarda kiracıya tazminat ödeme yükümlülüğü getirilmesi de düzenlemenin parçaları arasındaydı.

Böylece hükümetin birkaç gün önce açıkladığı ve konut krizine yönelik acil müdahale olarak sunduğu iki kararname de yürürlükten kalkmış oldu.

Öfke Meclis’in dışına taştı

Meclis’teki oylama, zaten haftalardır büyüyen konut öfkesini yatıştırmak bir yana, protestoların daha da büyümesine yol açtı.

items.title: Fransa'da liselilerin eylemleri büyüyor
summary_lines: 564 eğitim kurumu eylemden etkilendi, protestolar başlangıçtan ~5 bin kişi gözaltına alındı.
600'den fazla polis memuru yaralandı, 6 Ekim'de yeni eylem günü planlanıyor.
Hükümet, BTS ve hazırlık sınıflarında burslu olmayanlardan kayıt ücreti planından geri adım attı.
Öğrenci talepleri: öğretmen/personel eksikliği, kalabalık sınıflar, bakımsız binalar, Parcoursup.
items.why: Fransa'da lise eylemleri ülke geneline yayılıyor, hükümet tek adım geri çekti ama temel talepler karşılanmadı.
items.description:
Dış Haberler

Fransa'da liselilerin eğitim koşullarına karşı başlattığı eylemler ülke geneline yayılırken, öğrencilerin taleplerine eğitim emekçileri de destek veriyor. Hükümetin 2027 bütçesindeki kemer sıkma politikaları kamu çalışanlarının da tepkisini çekerken, 6 Ekim'de öğrenciler ve eğitim emekçilerinin katılacağı yeni bir eylem günü bekleniyor.

Fransa'da liselilerin haftalardır sürdürdüğü eylemler geri çekilmek bir yana ülke geneline yayılıyor. Paris banliyölerinde başlayan hareket, Lille'den Marsilya'ya, Lyon'dan Nîmes'e kadar çok sayıda kente ulaşırken farklı türden okullarda da eylemler düzenleniyor. 1 Ekim'de öğrenci örgütleri yaklaşık 30 üniversitenin de harekete destek verdiğini açıkladı.

2 Ekim Cuma günü eylemlerde kısmi bir gerileme yaşansa da Fransa basını hareketin sona erdiğine ilişkin bir işaret bulunmadığını aktardı. Gün ortasında 564 eğitim kurumunun eylemlerden etkilendiği bildirilirken, bazı okulların kapatılması üzerine öğrencilerin eylemlerini başka okullara taşıdığı görüldü.

 Desteklemek, güç vermek için tüm okurlarımızı soL Haber'e abone olmaya davet ediyoruz.

ABONE OL

 

Hükümetten sınırlı geri adım

Eylemlerin büyümesi üzerine Eğitim Bakanı Édouard Geffray, sendikalar, öğrenci temsilcileri ve velilerle görüşmeye başladı. Bakanlık, öğrencilerin talepleri konusunda "okul demokrasisi" üzerine çalışma yürütüleceğini açıkladı.

Hükümet ayrıca 2027 bütçesinde, öğrenci eylemlerinin önemli başlıklarından biri olan BTS ve hazırlık sınıflarındaki burs almayan öğrencilerden kayıt ücreti alınması planından geri adım attı.

Ancak öğrencilerin temel talepleri karşılanmış değil. Öğretmen ve personel eksikliği, kalabalık sınıflar, bakımsız okul binaları, ağır ders programları ve üniversiteye geçiş sistemi Parcoursup'a ilişkin sorunlar eylemlerin başlıca gündemlerini oluşturmaya devam ediyor.

Binlerce gözaltı, artan polis müdahalesi

Eylemler büyürken polis müdahaleleri de hareketin önemli başlıklarından biri haline geldi.

Protestoların başladığı pazartesiden bu yana yaklaşık 5 bin kişi gözaltına alındı. Gözaltına alınanların önemli bölümünün gençlerden oluştuğu bildirildi. 600'den fazla polis memurunun da yaralandığı aktarıldı.

Eylemlerin bazı kentlerde çatışmalara ve kamu mallarına zarar verilmesine dönüşmesi hükümet tarafından protestoların tamamına yönelik suçlamaların gerekçesi olarak kullanılırken, öğrenci ve eğitim örgütleri ise okullardaki koşulların ve gençlerin taleplerinin gündemden düşürülmemesi çağrısı yapıyor.

items.title: Girne'deki gemi faciasında bir kişinin daha cansız bedenine ulaşıldı
summary_lines: 30 Ağustos'ta Kuzey Kıbrıs Girne açıklarında batan 'Filo Jet' yüksek hızlı yolcu gemisinde ölü sayısı 19'a yükseldi.
9 kişi hâlâ kayıp, arama çalışmaları devam ediyor.
Kimlik tespiti için DNA çalışması başlatıldı.
items.why: Gemi kazası ölüm sayısını artırıyor, kalan 9 kayıp için arama devam ediyor.
items.description:
Haber Merkezi

Girne açıklarında meydana gelen gemi kazasının ardından başlatılan arama çalışmaları neticesinde bir cansız bedene daha ulaşıldığı duyuruldu, kimlik tespiti için DNA çalışmasının başlatıldığı belirtildi.

Kuzey Kıbrıs'ın Girne açıklarında 30 Ağustos'ta batan "Filo Jet" isimli yüksek hızlı yolcu gemisindeki kayıpları arama çalışmalarında bir kişinin daha cenazesine ulaşıldığı bildirildi.

Açıklama Kuzey Kıbrıs Başbakanlığı'nca yapıldı, kimlik tespiti için DNA çalışmasının başlatıldığı belirtildi.

 Desteklemek, güç vermek için tüm okurlarımızı soL Haber'e abone olmaya davet ediyoruz.

items.title: Washington'dan seçim öncesi savaş tehdidi, Tahran'dan Hürmüz yanıtı
summary_lines: Trump, 3 Kasım ara seçimleri öncesi İran'ı 'resmen yerle bir ettik' ve 'zor yoldan mı kolay yoldan mı halledeceğiz' dedi.

items.why: Seçim öncesi ABD-İran gerginliği tırmanıyor, Hürmüz Boğazı kontrolü doğrudan müzakere tahtasında.
items.description:
Dış Haberler

3 Kasım ara seçimleri öncesi Tahran'ı "süreci zor yoldan halletmekle" tehdit eden ABD Başkanı Donald Trump'a yanıt veren İran Meclis Başkanı Kalibaf, öne sürdükleri yedi şart kabul edilmeden Hürmüz Boğazı'nın kesinlikle açılmayacağını bildirdi.

İran'da ortaya attığı iddiaları yerine getiremeyen ABD Başkanı Donald Trump tehditlerine devam ediyor. Saldırılar için bir süredir 3 Kasım'da yapılacak ara seçimlerin sonrasını işaret eden Trump, İran konusunda karar verme aşamasında olduğunu öne sürdü ve "Tek soru şu: Biz bu süreci kolay yoldan mı yoksa zor yoldan mı halledeceğiz?" dedi.

İran ise Katar arabuluculuğunda ABD'ye sunduğu yedi şartın karşılanması konusunda kararlılığını sürdürüyor. İran Meclis Başkanı Muhammed Bakır Kalibaf, "İran'ın sunduğu yedi şart uygulanmadıkça Hürmüz Boğazı açılmayacak" dedi.

 Desteklemek, güç vermek için tüm okurlarımızı soL Haber'e abone olmaya davet ediyoruz.

ABONE OL

'İran konusunda karar verme noktasındayım'

ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, Ohio eyaletinde gerçekleştireceği miting için Beyaz Saray'dan ayrılırken basın mensuplarının sorularını yanıtladı.

Trump, 3 Kasım'da yapılacak Kongre ara seçimleri yaklaşırken İran'la savaş konusunda ABD'nin ne durumda olduğu yönündeki soruya şu yanıtı verdi:

"İran'ı resmen yerle bir ettik. Şimdi İran konusunda karar verme noktasındayım. Tek soru şu: Biz bu süreci kolay yoldan mı yoksa zor yoldan mı halledeceğiz?"

Trump, daha sonra yanıtladığı başka bir soruda da İran'ın "nükleer silah planlarından fiilen vazgeçtiğini" iddia etti.

'Sunulan yedi şart uygulanmadıkça Hürmüz Boğazı açılmayacak'

Öte yandan İran da sunduğu şartlar kabul edilmediği sürece Hürmüz Boğazı'nın açılmayacağını bildirdi.

İran resmi haber ajansı IRNA'nın aktardığına göre İran Meclis Başkanı Muhammed Bakır Kalibaf, Meclisin basına açık oturumunda gündeme ilişkin değerlendirmelerde bulundu.

ABD'nin medyada yer alan açıklamalarının aksine arabulucular üzerinden İran'a öneride bulunduklarını söyleyen Kalibaf, "Tek taraflı taleplerde bulunma döneminin bittiğini ve İran'ın sunduğu yedi şart uygulanmadıkça Hürmüz Boğazı'nın açılmayacağını bilmeleri gerekiyor" diye konuştu.

Kalibaf, ABD'nin İran'ın kararlılığını iyi bildiğini ve iç kamuoyunda algı oluşturmak için ekonomik baskı ve askeri girişimlere ilave olarak tehdit söylemlerini artırdığını belirtti.

Ülkesinin sosyal medyada yer alan tehdit içerikli açıklamalara göre değil gerçeklere göre politika belirlediğini söyleyen Kalibaf, ABD'nin yaptığı çelişkili açıklamaların İran halkının zihnini karıştırmayı amaçladığını dile getirdi.

İran heyeti, Birleşmiş Milletler (BM) Genel Kurulu marjında gittiği ABD'de, Hürmüz Boğazı'nın açılmasına ilişkin Katar arabuluculuğunda ABD'ye yedi şart sunmuştu. Ancak ABD Başkanı Donald Trump, İran'ın şartlarını kabul etmediklerini açıklamıştı.

items.title: Okuduğunu Neden Unutuyorsun?
summary_lines: Barış Özcan names his retention method «Unutkâr olmak», forgetting profitably, and says he will ask one question at the end that reveals why you remember what you read.
The video traces memory research from Ebbinghaus's meaningless-syllable experiments (1885) to Borges' Funes and the 1920s Moscow reporter Solomon Shereshevsky, who could not forget anything at all.
Cited sources include Bjork & Bjork 2019 (forgetting as a friend of learning), a 2025 Science study showing babies record memories, and Roediger & Karpicke 2006 on retrieval practice over rereading.
Full text and all sources are posted at barisozcan.com/yazi/okudugunu-neden-unutuyorsun [no transcript]
items.why: It reframes forgetting from a bug into a feature of how memory actually works.
items.description:
Bir kitabı çok beğenerek bitirip bir hafta sonra anlatmaya kalkınca iki cümlede tıkandığınız oldu mu? Bana çok oldu. Ben de okuduklarımızı neden unuttuğumuzu, unuttuklarımızın nereye gittiğini ve onları aklımızda nasıl tutabileceğimizi merak edip bu videoyu hazırladım. Videoda kendi kullandığım bir yöntemi de anlatıyorum, adını bile koydum: Unutkâr olmak, yani biraz unutmanın kârı.

Çayınızı, kahvenizi alın, size 1920'lerin Moskova'sında hiçbir şeyi unutamayan bir muhabirin hikâyesini anlatacağım. Oradan Ebbinghaus'un anlamsız hecelerine, bebek odamıza, ders alabilen bir böbrek hücresine ve Borges'in Funes'ine uzanıyoruz. Videonun sonunda da size bu hikâyeden tek bir soru soracağım. Not almanıza gerek yok, sadece izleyin. Cevabı hatırlarsanız nedenini de öğrenmiş olacaksınız.

2. İnce doğranmış soğan ve ezilmiş sarımsağı ekleyip yumuşayana kadar kavurmaya devam edin. Domates salçasını ilave edip kokusu çıkana kadar kısa süre kavurun.
3. Domates püresi, sıcak su, tuz, toz şeker, karabiber ve toz kırmızı biberi ekleyip karıştırın. Harcı tamamen suyunu çektirmeden, hafif sulu ve soslu kalacak şekilde birkaç dakika pişirip ocaktan alın.
4. Hamburger ekmeklerini ortadan ikiye bölüp kesik yüzeyleri yukarı bakacak şekilde fırın kabına yerleştirin.
5. Her ekmeğin içine  bir dilim burger peyniri koyun. Üzerlerine kıymalı harcı bolca paylaştırın.
6. Kıymalı harcın üzerine rendelenmiş kaşar peynirini serpiştirin ve ince kıyılmış maydanozu ekleyin.

items.title: Yoksa Palamutu Hala Aynı Şekilde Mi Pişiriyorsunuz? 😱 #yemekcom
summary_lines: Boil 2 whole bonito with 2 bay leaves, then strain the cooking water to use as stock for the pilav instead of discarding it.

items.why: Turns the fish-boiling water into the pilav's cooking liquid, so nothing goes to waste.
items.description:
Palamut mevsimindeyken onu bir de böyle denemeye ne dersiniz? 🐟🍅

@yaseminchef  palamudu önce defne yaprağıyla pişirip köfteye dönüştürüyor, lezzetli suyunu da domatesli pilavla buluşturuyor! Mis gibi palamut köfteleri ve balık suyuyla pişen tereyağlı domatesli pilav bir araya gelince tam mevsimlik, farklı bir akşam yemeği çıkıyor!!😋

Palamudu hep aynı şekilde pişirmek istemeyenler bu tarifi kaydetmeyi unutmasın!!

📝 Domatesli Pilav ve Palamut Köftesi
Hazırlama Süresi: 30 dakika
Pişirme Süresi: 40 dakika
Porsiyon: 4 kişilik

Malzemeler
Haşlamak İçin:
2 adet palamut
2 adet defne yaprağı
Üzerini geçecek kadar su

Palamut Köftesi İçin:
Haşlanmış ve kılçıkları ayıklanmış palamut
1 adet kuru soğan
1 adet yumurta
1/2 demet maydanoz
1 diş sarımsak
4 yemek kaşığı panko
1 adet limonun rendelenmiş kabuğu
1 çay kaşığı tuz
1/2 çay kaşığı karabiber
1/2 çay kaşığı kimyon
2 yemek kaşığı zeytinyağı

Domatesli Pilav İçin:
2 su bardağı pirinç
3 yemek kaşığı tereyağı
1 adet küçük boy kuru soğan
1 su bardağı domates püresi
2 su bardağı süzülmüş sıcak balık suyu
1 çay kaşığı tuz

Yapılışı
1. Palamutları temizleyip tencereye alın. Defne yapraklarını ve üzerini geçecek kadar suyu ekleyip balıklar pişene kadar haşlayın.
2. Palamutları sudan çıkarıp biraz soğumaya bırakın. Haşlama suyunu ince bir süzgeçten geçirerek tortularından tamamen ayırın ve pilavda kullanmak üzere kenara alın.
3. Soğuyan palamutların derisini ve tüm kılçıklarını dikkatlice ayıklayıp etlerini didikleyin.
4. Kuru soğan, yumurta, maydanoz, sarımsak, panko, limon kabuğu rendesi, tuz, karabiber ve kimyonu rondoya alın. Malzemeler iyice parçalanıp bütünleşene kadar rondodan geçirin.
5. Hazırladığınız karışımı didiklenmiş palamutlarla bir kaseye alın ve güzelce yoğurun. Harçtan parçalar alıp elinizle köfte şekli verin. Tavada zeytinyağını ısıtıp palamut köftelerini önlü arkalı güzelce kızartın.
6. Domatesli pilav için tereyağını tencerede hafifçe kahverengileşip fındıksı bir koku alana kadar ısıtın. İnce doğranmış soğanı ekleyip yumuşayana kadar kavurun.
7. Domates püresini ekleyip suyunu biraz çekene kadar pişirin. Yıkanmış ve süzülmüş pirinci ilave edip birkaç dakika kavurun.
8. Tuz ve sıcak balık suyunu ekleyip karıştırın. Kaynamaya başladığında ocağın altını kısın, kapağını kapatın ve pirinç suyunu çekene kadar pişirin.
9. Pilavı ocaktan aldıktan sonra 10 dakika dinlendirin. Domatesli pilavı palamut köfteleriyle birlikte sıcak servis edin. Afiyet olsun!

items.title: 1240: Anadolu'yu Sarsan O Büyük İsyan
summary_lines: 1240 is the title date for the Babai Revolt, which the description calls a critical turning point for the Anatolian Seljuk state.
Maps are used to trace 13th-century political fragmentation, weakened central authority, and the military and political dimensions of the Anatolian Seljuk crisis. [no transcript]
items.why: It gives a map-based entry point to the 1240 Babai Revolt and the weakening of Anatolian Seljuk central authority.
items.description:
Babai İsyanı, Anadolu Selçuklu Devleti'ni sarsan en kritik dönüm noktalarından biridir. Bu isyanın arka planına bakıyoruz.

Anadolu'nun siyasi haritaları sürekli değişirken, 13. yüzyılda meydana gelen Babai İsyanı bölgedeki dengeleri kökten değiştirdi. Bu videoda, haritalar üzerinden dönemin siyasi parçalanmışlığını ve merkezi otoritenin zayıfladığı o kritik süreci inceliyoruz. Anadolu Selçuklu Devleti'nin içine düştüğü bu büyük krizi, askeri ve siyasi boyutlarıyla ele alıyoruz.

Anadolu tarihi boyunca birçok ayaklanmaya sahne oldu ancak Babai hareketi, özellikle Türkiye Selçukluları üzerindeki etkisiyle farklı bir yere sahiptir. Bölgedeki güç boşluklarını ve farklı siyasi yapıların sınırlarını haritalarla detaylandırarak, bu isyanın Anadolu'nun kaderini nasıl çizdiğini anlamaya çalışıyoruz.

Kanalımıza abone olarak her hafta paylaştığımız tarih analizlerini takip edebilir, yorumlarda bir sonraki videoda hangi dönemi incelememizi istediğinizi belirtebilirsiniz.
